skill.title: Derive the mortgage repayment formula
skill.input: loan = sum of PVs of repayments
skill.example: P = A/(1 + i) + … + A/(1 + i)ᵗ ⇒ formula
needs: Find the repayment on a loan/mortgage
Sum n terms of a geometric series

note: Use the SAME method as the references (they are the lesson so far); change one thing, as usual. The method: Writes the loan as the sum of repayments in today's money, sums the geometric series algebraically and makes A the subject. Earlier backups were dropped for doing this instead: A numerical calculation of a repayment with a calculator, rather than deriving the formula algebraically.

steps.title: Write the loan as the sum of the repayments in today's money

lines.text: A repayment $A$ made at the end of period $k$ is worth $\frac{A}{(1+i)^k}$ today. Today's value of all $t$ repayments is the loan $P$.

steps.title: Use the sum of a geometric series

lines.text: This is a geometric series with first term $a = \frac{A}{1+i}$, common ratio $r = \frac{1}{1+i}$ and $t$ terms, so $S_t = \frac{a(1 - r^t)}{1 - r}$.

steps.title: Cancel the factor 1/(1+i) and tidy up

lines.text: Multiply both sides by $i(1+i)^t$, then divide both sides by $(1+i)^t - 1$.

steps.title: Write the loan as the sum of the repayments in today's money

lines.text: The first repayment is made now, so it is worth $A$. A repayment made after $k$ months is worth $\frac{A}{(1+i)^k}$ today.
Geometric with first term $a = A$, common ratio $r = \frac{1}{1+i}$ and $t$ terms.

steps.title: Divide by the fraction and tidy up

lines.text: Multiply both sides by $i(1+i)^{t-1}$, then divide by $(1+i)^t - 1$.

skill.title: Interpret f(x) = g(x) as a comparison of functions
skill.example: 2ˣ vs x² → equal at x = 2, 4 and x ≈ −0.77

note: Use the SAME method as the references (they are the lesson so far); change one thing, as usual. The method: Read a graph to find where two functions are equal or one is below the other. Earlier backups were dropped for doing this instead: Substitutes a value into two formulas and compares the outputs instead of reading where graphs cross or lie above each other. Calculates two charges from formulas and compares them rather than reading a graph.

lines.text: $m(x) = 0$ where the graph of $m$ meets the $x$-axis.

steps.title: Find where the two graphs cross

lines.text: The graphs of $k$ and $m$ cross at $x = 2$ and $x = 3.5$.

steps.title: Find where k(x) is less than m(x)

lines.text: Between $x = 2$ and $x = 3.5$ the graph of $m$ is above the graph of $k$.
Outside that range, $m$ is below $k$. Do not include the endpoints, because there $k(x) = m(x)$.
